note:
Reviewed CDB90 match 21, pinned revision e0b35ec4d798cec3bb4e6970c0f6bb7aa69e2f4c. CDB90 (CAA Database of Battles, Version 1990), tidy data maintained by Jeffrey B. Arnold. Original US Army Concepts Analysis Agency data; revised data licensed ODC-BY. Original force designations and strength interpretations are retained with each quantity. Each side is one aggregate force, including any coalition; its total is not allocated among members. Personnel casualties are not deaths. Source estimates and adjudged error margins are not statistical confidence intervals. Equipment and tactical movements are not established by this dataset. Match review: Derived actors incorrectly says Royalist for both rows. Original NAM distinguishes ENG ROY ARMY from ENG PARL ARMY. Keep the parliamentary/allied force local, without assigning its combined English/Scottish camp total to either Roundheads or Covenanters alone. Identity review (attacker; original CDB90 name ENG PARL ARMY): The Historic England report identifies the combined armies of the Scottish Covenanters, the Eastern Association and Lord Fairfax. This clarifies the original abbreviated ENG PARL ARMY designation without assigning the coalition total to any one constituent. The local ID, original source qualifier, side and quantitative estimates remain unchanged.

Equipment review for Marston Moor: the British Civil War pike model illustrates the Parliamentary infantry component of the combined English and Scottish allied army documented in the Historic England report. The National Army Museum armour supplies a period equipment analogy; its presence does not establish an exact regiment, national dress or a uniform armour distribution. No pike-to-musket ratio or infantry share of the whole allied force is inferred, and the local coalition ID, side and CDB personnel and loss estimates are unchanged.
